Recent findings suggest that SPOILER ALERT! This post contains some details from the first two episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3.

If there is one thing that the kids of Camp Half-Blood can count on, it’s that their lives are only going to get more complicated.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians returned to Disney+ for Season 3 on Friday, and already the dynamics have shifted. The first episode opens with Percy (Walker Scobell) and Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries) recruiting the recently revived child of Zeus, Thalia (Tamara Smart), to help them rescue two younger demigods — Nico and Bianca di Angelo, the children of Hades — and the tension is palpable. Related Stories Casting 'Afterlife With Archie' Disney+ Series Casts Its Archie, Veronica, Betty, Jughead & Sabrina News 'Gilmore Girls: A Year In The Life' Gets New Home On Hulu After Netflix Deal Ends, Release Date Set.

Industry observers note that “I think that Annabeth’s presence is actually incredibly divisive between the two of them,” Smart tells Deadline of the dynamic between Thalia and Percy. Watch on Deadline.

In terms of sowing that division on screen, she adds that “a lot of it is based in our actual relationship in the best of ways.”.

“Walker also has the exact same personality and sense of humor. So, right right off the bat, we were definitely going back and forth and joking, and I think the only thing we had to do was just up the stakes and be serious about it, which was actually more difficult than we planned,” she says.

Percy and Thalia can’t agree on almost anything, except their loyalty to Annabeth, who has unwittingly been thrown in the middle of their power struggle at the start of the season.

So, when Annabeth is captured and brought to an enemy stronghold where she’s forced to bear the weight of the sky (the eponymous Titan’s Curse), those two have to set aside their differences quite promptly.

According to recent reports, “She kind of kept them at a safe distance away from each other, because, as I guess we’ve seen the trailer, bad things happen when they’re not at that safe distance,” Scobell notes. “So I think without her there, they’re forced to actually work together and try to figure each other out and attempt to understand each other.”.

According to recent reports, adds Smart: “They actually have to be forced into proximity to work together to get her back, because that’s their mutual interest. So, it’s really beautiful in a way that her absence brings them closer, which is a very human thing for us. I think as people, we’re just always brought closer by tragedy. But I think that for them specifically, a lot of ego has to get out the door for them to work together to achieve their mutual goal.”.

Rather than put a wedge in Annabeth’s relationship with either, Jeffries thinks that the tension between Percy and Thalia also provides some clarity for the daughter of Athena. Whether she’s ready to face that realization yet is another story.

In a recent development, “I honestly feel like you get to see more Percabeth when it’s between Percy and Thalia,” Jeffries states. “I feel like her eyes open up a little bit. Annabeth is very smart. Even though she’s making it look like she’s not noticing, she knows [she’s developing feelings for Percy]. I don’t know if that’s more of like a denial between her of like, ‘No, no, I’m working right now. I’m on missions. I don’t have time to be falling in love…’.

She continues: “You get to see the fight [in her] more, not physically, but just like ‘No, I love this person. You’re not gonna take him away from me.'”.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (970 w)

Latest Update: Netflix’s ‘Minimum Wage’ Ushers In Streaming’s Short Ep Sitcom Era: “The Future Is 15-Minute ‘SpongeBob’-Length Episodes”

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a world of increasingly short attention spans, social media slop and doomscrolling brainrot, it’s a wonder why many television shows got longer in the streaming era.
  • Case in point, the 22-minute broadcast sitcom was largely replaced by the 30-minute dramedy and the 43-minute procedural has been overshadowed by the hour-long premium drama series.
  • Netflix, however, has found success with a much shorter concept in Minimum Wage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a world of increasingly short attention spans, social media slop and doomscrolling brainrot, it’s a wonder why many television shows got longer in the streaming era.

Case in point, the 22-minute broadcast sitcom was largely replaced by the 30-minute dramedy and the 43-minute procedural has been overshadowed by the hour-long premium drama series.

Netflix, however, has found success with a much shorter concept in Minimum Wage.

The comedy series, which comes from Jeremy Garelick and Will Phelps’ American High, consists of 14 episodes between 12 and 20 minutes in its first tranche, which debuted at the end of October.

Sources indicate that set in a pizza joint and starring new SNL darling Grace Reiter, Aidan Micho, Hyde Healy, Julia Dicesare, Luke Burke, Ryan Micho, Tommy Armstrong and Randall Park, its short episodes are a feature, not a bug. Watch on Deadline.

It has been revealed that phelps told Deadline, “The future is these 15-minute kind of SpongeBob-length episodes where it’s really fast. There’s not any fat.”.

In fact, Netflix demanded short episodes for the show, which began life as a series of YouTube sketches shot during the middle of the night with interns as camera operators and a building manager handling the boom mic.

Garelick said, “When we closed the deal, [Netflix] said that they wanted it to be a minimum of twelve and a half-minute episodes. It was an interesting challenge because most episodic TV reveals are 22 to 30 pages. It was almost like we were inventing a fresh structure as we were going and it was hard.”.

Episodes were also capped at 20 minutes with shooting scripts ending up being around 15 pages and the cast encouraged to improv. “You can captivate an audience for 15 minutes really well,” Phelps added. “Jeremy and I are coming at it from traditional screenplay writing and the cast is coming at it from making the most exciting one-minute thing for TikTok or Instagram.”.

This contrast is both the essence of Minimum Wage and also highlights one of the industry’s challenges as creators such as Druski and others are increasingly working on scripted projects for streamers.

“Everyone’s clamoring for creators to make shows now [following] the success of Obsession and Minimum Wage and I’m nervous that without the guidance of traditional screenwriters, you might fall into a trap of creators that are used to taking a one-minute premise and being told expand that into 15 minutes. That’s just going to be full of fat. Whereas we’re taking stories that really should be a half-hour and squeezing the fat out from the other side. That’s the secret sauce that we have.”.

Garelick began his career working as an assistant for Joel Schumacher and working on movies such as The Break-Up and The Wedding Ringer before teaming up with Phelps to buy a high school in upstate Newly introduced York, where they made films such as Banana Split, Holly Slept Over and Pete Davidson-starrer Massive Time Adolescence.

“We’ve become a traditional Hollywood studio, but we give a lot more trust to the creators and the artists, and we have an academy, our shorts and our sketch teams, and we’re kind of combining [it all],” mentioned Garelick.

Industry observers note that this also allowed American High to deliver more episodes of Minimum Wage than Netflix had originally ordered. The streamer initially greenlit 20 episodes but they ended up writing 28 scripts and persuaded Netflix that it would be cheaper to produce them all.

“We don’t get hung up on the actual business side of things. We’ll just do it for the love of the game,” added Phelps.

Minimum Wage debuted last month and reached Netflix’s global top ten charts with 2.4M views, impressive given the season’s run time is under four hours.

Recent findings suggest that it is one of a number of streaming shows keeping episode lengths concise. Shane Gillis’ Netflix comedy series Tires is generally in the 20-23-minute range, while HBO Max’s The Significant Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save The Universe consists of episodes between 18 and 20 minutes with one episode clocking in at only 15 minutes.

It has been revealed that co-creator Chuck Lorre, who has spent the vast majority of his career working in broadcast comedy, stated there was “no real reason” to pad the episodes. “The historic length of a show is entirely arbitrary, it comes from network television where a certain amount of advertising has to be sold to pay the way of making this television, but it’s not an element any longer in streaming,” Lorre said. “So, why not just make the best show we can and hope the audience is entertained and is not looking at their watch.”.

Minimum Wage works because it is a workplace comedy, one featuring an overwhelmed group of teenagers struggling to run The Slice Club, where the “stakes are low and the pressure is immense.”.

In a recent development, it’s not clear whether the remaining 14 episodes that American High shot will be labeled as the second part of season one or season two, but they are expected to air in spring 2027. There’s also plenty of road for more episodes; Garelick remarked that they’ve already got around 50 more draft scripts.

“It takes a few months to get there, and then it takes a year or so of incubating that online to get a fan base, and then you’re ready to start a show with some solid footing behind it, and the audience feels like they were part of the inception of this,” remarked Phelps. “I think it’s the future of TV.”.

Tech Report: This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first declared. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

Industry observers note that in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

It has been revealed that the simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you remarked) to your “Notes to self” note.

To take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

In a recent development, all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

It’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

In a recent development, there’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can strategy them better next time.

You’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

But this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I said it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of customers. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the firm has also introduced latest restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple unveiled plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give consumers more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Industry observers note that over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted latest job listings that offer a closer look at its looks to develop autonomous AI agents:.

According to recent reports, in one, Apple remarked it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “initiative and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Today’s report on the fresh job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring users to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the tech giant could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the fresh job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its aims for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how quickly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally launched its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

Gemini Notebook's New Interactive Site Builder Is Much More Useful Than I Expected

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • That might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • Industry observers note that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something fresh. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

That might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

Industry observers note that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

To make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

With a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but states you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

In a recent development, the finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a upcoming window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

Recent findings suggest that everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

For something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

In a recent development, I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

In a recent development, maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a major family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a new website.

Bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It has been revealed that it looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

The fresh stage production based on the 1987 film will arrive on Broadway this winter for a limited seven-month engagement. Performances begin Friday, February 12, 2027, at Broadway’s Lena Horne Theatre with a “gala celebration” on Sunday, March 14.

Birthright, beginning previews February 23 at the Hudson ahead of a March 15 opening, carries the imprimatur of a very successful and acclaimed Off Broadway run last summer, along with the reputation of the playwright – Jonathan Spector – who scored a major Broadway success last year with the Tony-winning Eureka Day. Casting for the play hasn’t been announced, but the Off Broadway production starred such New York stage favorites as Molly Ranson, Nate Mann, Liz Larsen, Eli Gelb, Molly Bernard, Zoë Winters and Hale Appleman.

March’s final weeks will continue the celebrity appeal with The Odd Couple, starring Steve Carell, who will play the persnickety Felix Ungar, and John C. Reilly, as the slob Oscar Madison. Hamilton‘s Thomas Kail directs at the Stephen Sondheim Theatre, with performances for the 15-week engagement beginning March 3, 2027, and an opening on March 23.

Sources indicate that and March goes out like a lion with Evita, director Jamie Lloyd’s revival of the Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber musical starring Rachel Zegler reprising her Olivier Award-winning performance as Eva Perón. Previews start February 27 at the Winter Garden – at the moment the home of Lloyd’s magnificent Much Ado – with an opening night of March 25.

Evita will be the final opening before the spring crunch of Tony-qualifying last minute arrivals goes full swing, and, yes, those shows will have plenty of stars as well – Jessica Chastain, Bryan Cranston, Laura Linney, Neil Patrick Harris and more. Those April openers include Gloria (April 5), Warriors (April 8), Purple Rain (April 12), All My Sons (April 13), The Sound of Music (April 15), Paddington The Musical (April 18), Montauk (April 19), Damn Yankees (April 20), Lost Lear (April 23) and Rhinoceros (April 25).

After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the organization is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with newly introduced privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several fresh features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Industry observers note that and speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing customers to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing latest tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful patch, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and consumers on the public beta can now try out these upcoming features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

CAA’s Bryan Lourd Urges Congress To Pass AI Legislation To Protect Americans “Famous Or Not”

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CAA chief Bryan Lourd is urging the full Congress to pass the No Fakes Act and deliver it to President Trump for signature, a move Lourd notes would protect everyone, famous or not, from nonconsensual digital replicas of their voices and likenesses.
  • In a guest essay published in today’s New York Times, Lourd writes, “The Senate and House should move promptly and deliver the bill to President Trump for signature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CAA chief Bryan Lourd is urging the full Congress to pass the No Fakes Act and deliver it to President Trump for signature, a move Lourd notes would protect everyone, famous or not, from nonconsensual digital replicas of their voices and likenesses.

In a guest essay published in today’s New York Times, Lourd writes, “The Senate and House should move promptly and deliver the bill to President Trump for signature. That would ensure Americans retain control of their images and voices in the A.I. era.”.

The No Fakes Act was approved unanimously by the Senate Judiciary Committee in June, and, Lourd contends, there “is momentum to pass it through the full Congress before the end of the year.” He calles it “one of the few A.I. bills with true bipartisan support.” Watch on Deadline.

Hollywood, Lourd writes, “is not afraid of latest technology.”.

According to recent reports, “The objection from actors, musicians and other creators is to a world in which anyone can use their face or voice without permission,” he writes. “In fact, many artists are already embracing A.I. on their own terms. Some of them are making deals with companies that are creating their A.I. likenesses, with their consent.”.

Lourd poses the problem as not just for Hollywood. “A content creator learned on her honeymoon that a YouTube ad was using an A.I. version of her to sell erectile dysfunction supplements,” he writes. “Is all this legal? Right now, it’s an open question. But it shouldn’t be.”.

In a recent development, “Hollywood doesn’t need America’s leaders to devise a newly introduced concept for new circumstances,” writes the chief executive and co-chairman of Creative Artists Agency. “We need them to extend and enforce the rules that already exist. The use of Americans’ faces, voices, performances and creative works is already subject to rules at the federal or state level that say, in short: You need to get permission, and you need to pay for the use.”.

Recent findings suggest that “This principle has guided the entertainment industry for more than a century,” he continues. “Whether it can continue to protect Americans may be decided in the coming weeks. The No Fakes Act would create a federal prohibition on creating nonconsensual digital replicas of any person’s voice or likeness — famous or not.”.

It has been revealed that the No Fakes Act, Lourd says, “would apply a tried-and-true formula to the A.I. era: control, consent and compensation. It would set a uniform federal standard to replace outdated, ill-fitting state laws, many of them written with an analog world in mind. Its supporters include all sides of the table: SAG-AFTRA, the union representing actors and other performers; the Motion Picture Association, representing the studios; and tech companies including IBM, Google and OpenAI.”.

Earlier this month, Lourd told Deadline’s Dominic Patten, that the issues around AI are “about the fundamental relationship between technological progress and creative rights, and who determines the value of creative work, who decides how that work is used, and whether creators will share in the opportunities AI creates.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer. But if your lesbian-forward supernatural horror series isn't drawing cries of "blasphemy!"...what are you even doing? In that spirit, we'll conjure up some other demonstrates dealing with the (extremely) dark side of high school.

It has been revealed that this time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate. There are ambiguous teases of the supernatural here (much more ambiguous than in The Body), but there's plenty of human-level horror as well. The show explores the nasty things we get up to when in survival mode (whether trapped in the wilds, stuck with other teenagers—or god forbid both at once), while also cynically (but accurately) positing that there's a huge difference between the version of the past we talk about and the one that really happened. Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

Situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It quickly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Sources indicate that juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

In a recent development, A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

According to recent reports, mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that swiftly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

Peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

The newly introduced Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

It has been revealed that four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

Adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing. Keeping that support as you change position is another. LiberNovo’s Dynamic Support System links the neck support, backrest, armrests, and seat so they move together as you recline.

It has been revealed that the Bionic FlexFit Backrest adds eight flexible panels that contour independently. Rather than relying on a single rigid backrest, the design lets different sections follow your back as you shift or turn. Omni Pro and Maxis Airflow add Active AirFlow seat ventilation. A fan draws air through the cushion to carry heat away, and an occupancy sensor pauses the fan when you stand up. These models also include a larger 3,000 mAh rechargeable battery.

Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar’s Film Committee

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Watermelon Pictures and the Film Committee at Media City Qatar have revealed a planned strategic partnership to develop and co-produce a slate of films telling stories from the Global South.
  • For Watermelon, the partnership marks a significant expansion into larger-scale, mainstream production.
  • Badie Ali and Hamza Ali released their Chicago-based production and distribution firm in 2024, with a mission to amplify Palestinian and other under-represented voices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watermelon Pictures and the Film Committee at Media City Qatar have revealed a planned strategic partnership to develop and co-produce a slate of films telling stories from the Global South.

For Watermelon, the partnership marks a significant expansion into larger-scale, mainstream production.

Badie Ali and Hamza Ali released their Chicago-based production and distribution firm in 2024, with a mission to amplify Palestinian and other under-represented voices.

Sources indicate that until now, the company has focused mainly on distribution, with recent releases including The Voice of Hind Rajab, El Sett, Who Killed Alex Odeh? and American Doctor. Related Stories News Egyptian Music Star Mohamed Mounir Gets Biopic - Doha Industry Days News 'Al Hayba' Star Taim Hasan To Play Syrian Whistleblower Farid Al-Madhhan In Neon-Backed 'Caesar' Biopic.

Sources indicate that its cofounders recently signaled to Deadline that they were working on a development slate, without going into detail. Watch on Deadline.

The strategic partnership aims to combine Qatar’s infrastructure and resources as it seeks to grow the film and TV sector at home and regionally, and Watermelon’s access to leading talent, established distribution infrastructure, and understanding of what resonates with audiences.

“When we founded Watermelon Pictures, our vision was to bring powerful stories to the big screen with an unwavering commitment to authenticity,” noted Watermelon Pictures cofounder Badie Ali.

“Our partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar is a major step toward realizing that promise, allowing us to tell these stories on a larger scale while remaining true to the people and places at their heart.”.

Under the partnership, the parties would aim to shoot projects substantially in Qatar or structure them as Qatari co-productions.

They would also seek to involve Doha-based post-production companies and help eligible projects access the Qatar Screen Production Incentive (QSPI), creating opportunities for local crews, businesses, and creative talent while strengthening Qatar’s position as an international production hub.

“Through this partnership, we want to give filmmakers the resources to tell stories rooted in their communities and bring them to audiences around the world. We also want the films we support to create work for crews and businesses in Qatar and give them experience they can carry into their next production,” mentioned Hassan Al Thawadi, Chairman of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar.

Sources indicate that the Film Committee and Watermelon Pictures will jointly identify projects for the initial slate. The proposed partnership is subject to definitive agreements and the required approvals, with projects to be considered individually. More details on specific projects are soon to be confirmed.

“Too many compelling stories and perspectives, including those of Arab and Muslim communities, have historically been underrepresented in mainstream cinema. We see an enormous opportunity to change that. Our planned slate will span genres, challenge perceptions, and, above all, entertain. Our ambition isn’t simply to create space in the industry. It’s to compete at its highest level,” stated Watermelon Pictures cofounder Hamza Ali.

The announcement of the planned partnership was made during the Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days, running from November 19 to 21 within the framework of the Doha Film Festival.

If You Loved 'Yellowjackets,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying.
  • Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.
  • In a recent development, the survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yellowjackets is a vibe. The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying. The dual timelines build tension around the story’s many mysteries, and the complex characters (no one’s completely good or evil on this show) make for a lot of surprising plot swerves that feel grounded despite the supernatural implications all around them. If you’re looking for more of that specific flavor of horror, you should probably watch Alive.

Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.

In a recent development, the survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances. They use the wrecked plane as shelter in the withering cold, they scavenge for anything that could be useful, and they ration out the only food they have: Some chocolates and a case of wine. But an early mistake leaves them without any food at all, and slowly they come to the sickening realization that their best chance at survival is to treat the corpses of their friends and families scattered around the crash site as a food source.

Sources indicate that there’s no supernatural aspect, but the story has a similar tone of desperation and despair as Yellowjackets. These are people determined to survive in an impossible situation, and they do things that no one outside of their shared experience could possibly understand. The real-life origins of the story add a sense of horror that more than matches the fictional “It” that haunts the girls of Yellowjackets; putting yourself into that very real experience makes it clear just how terrified everyone was. Rent Alive on Prime Video.

If you’re craving more cannibals, cults, and crazies at the mercy of nature itself, here are a few more movies you should check out.

In a recent development, if you want to watch a movie that is essentially an adaptation of Yellowjackets, check out Eden. Even though it was released years before the show, the stories are so similar (albeit largely gender-flipped) that the producers of Eden actually sued, claiming plagiarism (they lost). In the film, a men’s soccer team (and two women on the same plane) crash-land on a deserted island, and as they fight for survival, things descend into, yes, madness and cannibalism as the survivors suffer dwindling food and water supplies and the rise of two violently opposed factions. It’s not nearly as deeply imagined as Yellowjackets, and it doesn’t have the supernatural hints of the show, but if you want a truly similar story, it’s a good choice. Stream Eden on The Roku Channel, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that you obviously cannot discuss Yellowjackets without discussing Lord of the Flies, William Golding’s 1954 novel about a group of schoolboys who descend into brutality and savagery when they’re stranded on a deserted island. The book has been adapted many times, but the 1963 version directed by Peter Brook is still the best version. Brook managed to elicit remarkably naturalistic performances from his young actors, giving the story a realistic tone that is somehow more terrifying than any amount of horror vibes. Stream Lord of the Flies on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, A slower and more haunting story, Picnic at Hanging Rock explores some of the same themes as Yellowjackets in an entirely different way. On Valentine’s Day in the year 1900, several students and teachers from an all-girls private school in Victoria, Australia, head to Hanging Rock for a picnic. Four students head off to explore and fall inexplicably asleep, and then three vanish, along with one of the teachers. Dreamy and drenched in dread, the story never offers any easy answers, and it explores themes of invading natural areas where you’re not wanted, burgeoning (and confusing) adolescent sexuality, and how our fear of the unknowable warps our perspective and often diminishes our humanity. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, you can never really go wrong with a Hitchcock film, and if you’re looking for another story about a disparate group of people forced to make terrifying decisions in order to survive, watch Lifeboat (based on a story by John Steinbeck). One of the director’s most underrated films, it’s the story of a group of survivors in a lifeboat after a German U-boat sinks their ship during World War II (including one survivor from the German boat). It’s a masterful suspense engine that’s not afraid to have its characters discuss the moral and ethical quandaries facing them as they struggle to survive and maintain their humanity under a constant threat of death. Stream Lifeboat on Hoopla or rent it on Prime Video.

If you love the supernatural aspects of Yellowjackets as the girls come to believe a force they call “It” is out in the woods, check out The Ritual. Four friends embark on a hike in the wilds of northern Sweden to honor their deceased friend. When one of them is injured, they leave the marked trail to take a shortcut through the forest—where they are soon forced to shelter in an abandoned cabin, just like the Yellowjackets—and things begin to slide into the terrifying when they encounter a cult worshipping an ancient deity that grants them immortality in exchange for human sacrifices. It’s as if the show was condensed to an hour-and-a-half and the terror quotient was turned way, way up. Stream The Ritual on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp customers: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the newly introduced limit is rolling out to people on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

In a recent development, whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the enhancement becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company declared four newly introduced features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

With so many games now too massive for cartridges (leading to the controversial Game Key cards that are basically just a download key), it’s worth reiterating just how hefty some Switch 2 titles can be.

Launch titles like Street Fighter 6 and Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition came in at 60GB, but things have got progressively more storage-hungry from there.

According to recent reports, NBA 2K26 is over 70GB, EA Sports FC 27 is 75GB, and WWE 2K26 is 86GB, while the two Final Fantasy VII Remake titles are around 90GB each. That’s on top of launches this year like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, and many more.

Honestly, the Switch 2 has grown to become a haven for great third-party titles, and even if you’ve not invested in fresh storage space, you’ll no doubt find it very welcome as more games arrive, like FromSoftware’s Duskbloods, Maneater 2, and Xenoblade Genesis in 2027.

Sources indicate that amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

Sources indicate that if Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

Unlike Sony’s recent theatrical release of The Social Reckoning, which arguably didn’t resonate with the current tech era we’re living in, Neon is unwrapping Luca Guadagnino‘s Artificial about Open AI co-founders Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever and Elon Musk at a time when we fear the technology will end us.

Now whether that’s in regards to our existence or our financial livelihoods is another question.

Earlier this week, former OpenAI alum and Altman rival Dario Amodei’s Anthropic went public creating a $1.18 trillion manufacturer. However, shares fell from its $111 day-of-market price to $88.91 EOD Friday. Neon is shrewdly opening Artificial limited on Christmas Day (the perfect time to launch a sophisticated adult skewing awards contender), and in the run-up to that release, following premieres at Newly introduced York Film Festival and BFI London Film Fest, along with current awards voter screenings, anticipation is boiling for the pic evident in its current 95% fresh Rotten Tomatoes critics rating. Related Stories News Timothée Chalamet Addresses Possibility Of A 'Call Me by Your Name' Sequel: "Never Say Never" News Sam Altman On 'Artificial' Movie About Him -- Not Among "Ten Weirdest Things In My Life" Right Now.

As a filmmaker who knows something about love with the Zendaya starring tennis love triangle pic, Challengers, and Oscar winning gay romance, Call Me By Your Name, we spoke with Guadagnino on the latest Crew Call as to what pulled him into the OpenAI-verse. Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that take a listen below. Essentially, it’s about about a bunch of young mad, narcissistic scientists acting like flawed Greek Gods in San Francisco:.

Sources indicate that well before its theatrical release, Artificial generated a lot of controversy as its original studio, Amazon MGM Studios, backed away from the movie out of fear of OpenAI. That’s because Amazon has a $50 billion investment in the Altman non-profit.

In a recent development, however, unlike the Facebook camp back when Social Network was getting released in 2010, there’s been zero ill will coming from Altman or OpenAI about Guadaganino’s film. In fact, you could say they’re great sports.

Recent findings suggest that in a sit-down with the Vanity Fair podcast, Altman claims he “did not” coerce Amazon to drop Artificial. “I don’t know anyone else who did,” he added, “I didn’t speak to Jeff Bezos.”.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, Guadagnino brazenly shot the pic outside Altman’s house in San Francisco. The filmmaker tells us about that. For Altman, he was giddy about running into his onscreen doppelgänger, Andrew Garfield: “One morning, I was walking down the street to get coffee and there were all these cameras and there was a guy dressed exactly like me with the same backpack, walking so much, I felt like I was in a weird glitch or a simulation.”.

Altman emphasized to Vanity Fair that Garfield “did walk like me.”.

While Altman hasn’t seen Artificial, his reaction to the trailer is, “I don’t think they’re going for accuracy, so in that sense it doesn’t bother me. They’re trying to make a good movie and maybe it will be good. It won’t be good as an accurate depiction, except for the walk. I’m sure they’ll get other parts right at least accidentally.”.

One of the jaw dropping moments shown in the Artificial trailer is Altman having a bunker in his wine country estate loaded with guns.

“That is an example of an inaccuracy,” Altman told Vanity Fair, “There’s no bunker with firearms on the wall.”.

“I have a survivalist mindset,” Altman admitted, “but I don’t have a setup that is depicted in that trailer.”.

Guadagnino tells Deadline, “I have validated the validating information that has been vetted: He does have guns.”.

While the filmmaker experienced zero pushback from OpenAI and Altman during production on the Simon Rich script, he says “We were very careful that everything that was in the movie had to be approved legally, so that we were not bending facts and reality for our narrative purposes. But, because the truth in this case is more extraordinary than any fiction, that was okay. Because we had the drama, we had the juice.”.

When it came to Amazon exiting Artificial, Guadagnino had a Zen mindset: “I was cool because I like disruptions, very much.”.

“Their decision to give the movie to us to find another home was truly honorable, because they could have written off the movie and (stated) ‘Bye-bye’.”.

As far as Artificial being a hot potato that no studio wanted to handle, except NEON, Guadagnino asserts that “All the speculation about nobody wanting the movie; I like to think that there was the need (by the media) to fill blank pages with nothing.”.

Recent findings suggest that for off the bat, per Guadagnino, NEON was first, front and center in their passion to takeover the project after CAA screened it for them. Listen above for more details.

When it comes to the paranoia out there that AI is the catalyst for human extinction in ten years, the filmmaker tells Deadline, “I don’t have trust and I don’t have faith in humans.”.

According to recent reports, his suspicions about AI stem from growing up during the Cold War. “I remember very well in 1985 when Chernobyl happened,” he adds.

And there’s myriad reasons for concerns about AI, from a Chatbot being at the center of 16-year old Adam Raine’s suicide, to AI trespassing and impostering another tech giant’s security space.

We also talk with the Call Me By Your Name Best Picture Oscar nominee on why Andrew Garfield was the right guy to play Altman, and the Open AI Boss’ sincerity when it comes to creating guardrails for the technology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

Sources indicate that if you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the manufacturer is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

The standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Industry observers note that amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

In a recent development, A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

It has been revealed that amazon Health: Prime consumers get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance plans, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV reveals, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers new free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 is presently in beta testing with developers and public beta users. The update includes multiple upcoming features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 ….

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Industry observers note that as my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone customers sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final enhancement.

Sources indicate that the redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 consumers, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

Industry observers note that for Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week aims based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

In a recent development, reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a newly introduced face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Sources indicate that finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

It has been revealed that this includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The enhancement also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the revision expands Siri AI with many latest capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these upcoming capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so people can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

According to recent reports, there are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

Recent findings suggest that with iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test fresh ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple indicates it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to fresh languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

It has been revealed that you can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ blueprint, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

iOS 27.3 is a major patch to Safari. First, the update adds support for a fresh vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

Sources indicate that for Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The enhancement also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

According to recent reports, there are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Recent findings suggest that second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Here are a few other changes in iOS 27.3:.
